findings.issue: solc 0.8 advances the free-memory pointer by ceil32(return_data.size) after each call, so from the second call on every call's arguments and every event's data are raw memory (P2: 411 lines; 401 unnamed calls against 86 named, 18 events with raw data), although each argument was stored two lines earlier at the pointer's symbolic value.
findings.rule: Track memory relative to the symbolic free-memory pointer: after mem[64] = p + ceil32(rds), a store at p + ceil32(rds) + k is at mem[64] + k, so mem[mem[64] len n] is the stored words, and the call or log is printed with its selector's name and its arguments.

findings.source: AaveFoldStrategy.sol:498-502 uint256 requiredCollateral = borrowed.mul(_denom).div(collateralFactorNumerator()); uint256 toRepay = borrowed.sub(newBorrowTarget); uint256 toRedeem = Math.min(supplied.sub(requiredCollateral), amount.add(toRepay));
findings.issue: The division (Panic 18 on a zero collateralFactorNumerator) and the subtraction run before the addition (Panic 17) in the bytecode, but the text puts SafeMath.add first in one expression with the division nested in the second argument; read left to right, a zero collateralFactorNumerator with an overflowing amount + toRepay reverts with Panic(17) in the text and Panic(18) in the bytecode. The same loop in withdrawToVault (5230-5237) keeps the checks in the right order as separate tests.
findings.rule: When folding reverting checks into one expression, keep their order: an operand whose check comes first in the bytecode must be evaluated first in the text (or the checks stay as separate guarded tests in their order).

summary: Faithful structure with all five source loops shown as readable whiles, but the large functions are mostly unnamed raw-memory calls and events because the free-memory pointer becomes symbolic after each call; plus distributed borrow-target arithmetic, invariant loop variables and one reordering of reverting checks inside a min().
